# Handoff: graph view redesign ("M stripes as flow")

Written Sun 11 Oct 2026, 08:57. **Feature freeze is 10:00 and submission is 12:00** (`README.md` §1).

## 1. Focus

Design and build the **graph view** in the approved design language. The graph is the product's
centerpiece. The user's words: "the graph data structure IS our focus and selling point, it has to
look good (something like obsidian maybe)".

- **The direction is already decided** (§5: chain columns, stripes on the active chain,
  ink-on-paper cards). Build it into `gui/`: the cytoscape canvas plus the panels around it.
- After that comes the third page, the "in-between" view while a project runs. The user expects it
  to mostly follow from the start page and the graph view, plus the existing PM-loop logic.

## 2. Current state

- **Branch `feat/pm-inbox`, pushed to origin** (08:55). Checkpoints are on GitHub.
  - `1649980`: the new start screen.
  - `02663dd`: `gui/DESIGN.md`, the design language.

  It sits on `4d1a689` (PM loop) on top of `dev` (`c14a4be`). It is **not merged** into `dev` or
  `main`.
- **Start screen is done and approved** ("this is SOUND").
  - Files: `gui/start.js`, `gui/start.css`. Preview: http://localhost:8000/ui/?start
  - Verified in Chrome at 1280 and 500 px width.
  - The Start path was tested against the test DB with the agent call mocked. The brief and the
    source were written correctly.
- **The rest of the GUI is still the old look:** `gui/style.css`, `gui/app.js`, light slate/blue,
  rounded chips, four stacked header bars.
  - Its problems are listed in `handoff-pm-workbench-design-20261011-074435.md` → "Design problems
    already seen". Example: node text is about 5 px at zoom 0.42, and the header takes 214 px.
- **Tests green:** backend 26, agent-loop 16, GUI layout check.
- **Live DB `decision_graph`:** 17 nodes, 3 requirements, brief `NOTE-001`. It's good design
  material, so don't wipe it.

## 3. Key context & decisions

- **Read `gui/DESIGN.md` first.** It holds the colors, type, stripe-drawing rules, motion, and the
  "don't" list.
  - Reference implementation: `curve()` (offsets along the curve's normal) and the spring code in
    `gui/start.js`.
  - Reference images: `../reference1.jpg` (Sankey on warm paper), `../reference2.jpg` (M stripes),
    `../reference3.pdf` (the user's sketch of stripes fanning out to choices).
- **How the start page was designed, which the user liked:**
  - The user gave the theme (M stripes plus Sankey) and a sketch.
  - I built it straight away, then iterated from screenshots.
  - Visual fixes made along the way: stripes must not cross (assign them in order); they must not
    thin on bends (normal offset); they must not overlap text at phone width.
- **The user asked for Apple design principles** from
  https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills/blob/main/skills/apple-design/SKILL.md (a copy is in the
  session scratchpad). DESIGN.md already distils the parts we use: springs, interruptibility,
  typography and restraint.
- **Font:** BMW Type Next is licensed. It's used if installed locally or put in `gui/fonts/`
  (gitignored); otherwise the system font. Don't hotlink it from BMW servers. 404s for
  `fonts/*.woff2` in the console are expected.
- **Constraints (unchanged):**
  - Plain HTML/CSS/JS with no build step, cytoscape 3.30.2 from cdnjs, no new frameworks
    (`README.md` §4).
  - Keep the teammate (Alex0ir) features working: right-click menus, drag-to-connect, audit
    timeline, steering buttons, inbox and focus mode.
  - The brief is not drawn as a node.
  - Don't spend design space on scores (the user de-prioritised scoring).
- **Agent gotcha:** `agent-loop/loop.py` hardcodes `API_BASE = http://localhost:8000`. A server on
  another port still makes the agent write to the **live** DB. To test GUI flows on a test server,
  mock `/agent/*` in the browser. For example, `navigate_page` with an `initScript` that stubs
  `fetch` for `/agent/`.

## 4. Environment

- **Postgres 16** runs as a brew service (`brew services start postgresql@16`).
  - DBs: `decision_graph` (live) and `decision_graph_test`.
  - User and password are the defaults in `docker-compose.yml`.
- **Live server:** port 8000 (may still be running; check with `lsof -ti tcp:8000 -sTCP:LISTEN`).
  To start it:

  ```bash
  cd backend && set -a && . ../.env && set +a && .venv/bin/python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
  ```

  `.env` holds `OPENAI_API_KEY=<REDACTED>` and `OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-6-luna`. GUI changes need only a
  browser hard reload.
- **Safe test server** (test DB, no key, so the agent is rule-based, but see the gotcha above):

  ```bash
  cd backend && env -u OPENAI_API_KEY DATABASE_URL=postgresql://kolosok:<REDACTED>@localhost:5432/decision_graph_test .venv/bin/python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001
  ```

- **Tests:**
  - `node --check gui/app.js && node --check gui/start.js && node gui/layout.test.mjs`
  - backend: `DATABASE_URL=…/decision_graph_test .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`. Never run it
    against the live DB: it truncates.
  - `cd agent-loop && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`
- **Visual checks:** chrome-devtools MCP (`new_page` with `isolatedContext`, `resize_page`
  1280×800, `evaluate_script`).
  - Screenshots cost a lot of context, so use `jpeg` at quality 50–60 and only to judge visuals.
  - `showHint()` strips `?start` from the URL, so a reload loses preview mode; navigate to
    `?start` again.

## 5. Graph-view decisions (made by the user at 09:00, so build these; don't re-ask)

1. **Layout: chain columns, flowing.** Keep the left-to-right stages (Source → Evidence → Claim →
   Requirement, `gui/layout.js`), styled like a Sankey.
   - Rejected: an Obsidian force layout (chains hard to read, layout changes every run) and a
     hybrid (dots when zoomed out).
2. **Edges: stripes on the active chain.**
   - Every link is a thin `--ghost` line.
   - The selected or focused chain lights up as the three M stripes flowing through its nodes,
     exactly like the start page.
   - Rejected: every edge as stripes (too busy past about 20 nodes) and plain ink lines.
3. **Nodes: ink-on-paper cards.**
   - Same look as the start page options: a 2px ink top rule, then an uppercase type label with
     the id (`CLAIM · CLM-001`), then a 2-line title.
   - Approved or selected nodes become a solid ink card with white text.
   - Readable on a projector.
   - Rejected: Obsidian dots with labels, and cards that turn into dots.
   - Still to design in this language: how rejected, postponed, stale and waiting states look.
     Suggestion: use rule color or style and a small uppercase tag, not tinted fills.

**Implementation hint:** cytoscape can't draw three parallel offset stripes natively. One option
is to draw the active-chain stripes in an SVG overlay above the canvas, synced to
`cy.on("render viewport")` and reusing `curve()` from `start.js`. The other is three cytoscape
edges per link, with `source-endpoint`/`target-endpoint` offsets of ±10px. Prototype whichever is
faster, then check that stripes stay parallel at zoom.

## 6. Still open for the user

- When to merge `feat/pm-inbox` into `dev`, then `dev` into `main`. Judges see `main`; the team's
  TODO #1 is a second-laptop check.

## 7. Next steps

1. Load the live graph at 1280×800 to see the current state. The direction is decided (§5), so
   start building.
2. Move the design tokens (`--paper`, `--ink`, `--m-*`, `--type`) from `.start` in
   `gui/start.css` into a shared `:root` (for example `gui/theme.css`), so the workbench can use
   them.
3. Restyle the cytoscape stylesheet in `gui/app.js` (the `style:` array around lines 38–62):
   - paper background, square nodes;
   - readable labels (id plus a short title, larger font, maybe smaller `DX` in `gui/layout.js`);
   - stripe or ghost edges;
   - verdicts in the DESIGN.md language.
4. Slim the four header bars into one bar in the new style, and restyle the inbox and detail
   panel to match.
5. Re-run the demo flow (start → run agent → click requirement → approve → challenge → audit
   timeline) and the three test suites. Commit with the Entire checkpoint check, then push.

## 8. Suggested skills

- `ecc:frontend-design-direction` or `ecc:make-interfaces-feel-better`: when polishing the graph
  view against DESIGN.md.
- `dataviz`: before restyling the graph canvas (marks, color, legend rules).
- `/run`: to launch the app and click through the demo flow after the restyle.
- `/code-review`: before pushing the graph-view commit.
- `/handoff`: at the end of the session.

# kolosok-rehack — AI Development Guidelines

Team **Kolosok** at the **European Hackathon League (EHL) Grand Finale**, Munich (TUM.ai).
This file is the rulebook for every AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) and human working in this repo.
**Read it fully before your first change.** Human setup (GitHub token, credentials) lives in `README-Human`.

Source: [EHL Finale – All you need to know](https://tum-ai.notion.site/REDACTED)

---

## 0. Hard rules (non-negotiable)

1. **Entire must be enabled and every commit must carry a checkpoint.** The organisers will reject a submission that does not use Entire. No Entire → no valid submission.
2. **All work goes through git and gets pushed to `origin`.** Nothing that exists only on one laptop counts.
3. **`main` must always be demo-able.** We have a strict 6-minute slot for pitch + demo + questions.
4. **Never commit secrets** (API keys, tokens, `.env`). Entire redacts secrets in session logs, but do not rely on that.
5. **Never rewrite pushed history** (no `push --force`, no amending/rebasing pushed commits, no deleting `entire/*` branches or refs). Checkpoints are tied to commits; rewriting history can orphan them.

## 1. Key times (Munich local time)

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10 Oct, 11:00–11:30 | Entire technical onboarding |
| **Sat 10 Oct, 13:00** | **Challenge selection deadline** (captain, on https://ehl.gg/) |
| Sat 13:30 → Sun 12:00 | Hacking |
| **Sun 11 Oct, 12:00** | **Submission deadline** — hard stop |
| Sun 12:00–14:30 | Challenge pitches (6 min incl. Q&A) |
| Sun 15:30–16:30 | Main-stage final (6 teams) |

Internal targets: **feature freeze Sun 10:00**, first full submission by **Sun 10:30**, final re-submission by **11:45**.
Submissions can be repeated as often as we like before the deadline, so submit early and update.

**Challenge:** BMW Group — AI for Product Decision Making: an app that turns customer feedback, product/sales data and web research into prioritized, PM-reviewed customer requirements with a full audit trail. Details: [`BMW-Challenge.md`](BMW-Challenge.md).

## 2. Setup checklist (each machine, once)

Prerequisites: `git` on `PATH` (Entire shells out to it — it fails with `exec: "git": executable file not found` otherwise).

```bash
# 1. Install Entire (bash / Git Bash). On Windows the binary ends up in ~/.local/bin/entire.exe
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash

# 2. On the main branch of this repo:
git checkout main && git pull
git config pull.rebase true      # plain `git pull` makes merge commits, which carry no checkpoint
entire login                     # if not logged in yet
entire enable                    # enables session tracking in this repo
entire agent add claude-code     # install hooks for your agent; `entire agent list` shows others (codex, cursor, …)

# 3. Verify
entire status
entire doctor                    # if anything looks off
```

**You are set up correctly when** your next commit prints:

```
[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done
```

If you don't see that line, stop and fix Entire before writing more code.

## 3. Git workflow

- **Commit small and often** — at least every meaningful step, ideally every 15–30 min of agent work. Each commit becomes a checkpoint linking the code to the prompt/reasoning behind it.
- **Commit only from within a tracked agent session**, after the agent made the change with its file-edit tools. Hand-made commits, merge commits and shell (`sed`, `echo >`) edits get no checkpoint.
- **After every commit** check the checkpoint is there: `git log -1 --format=%B` must show an `Entire-Checkpoint:` line. If it is missing, fix it *before* pushing.
- **Commit messages:** imperative, prefixed by area, e.g. `feat(api): add route planner endpoint`, `fix(ui): handle empty results`, `docs: update run instructions`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `chore`, `test`, `demo`.
- **Sync before push:** `git pull --rebase` on *unpushed* local commits only, then `git push`. Resolve conflicts, never discard teammates' work.
- **Branches:** short-lived feature branches (`feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`) merged back to `main` quickly (within a few hours). Trivial fixes may go straight to `main`. Do not let branches drift overnight.
- **Do not commit:** `.env`, credentials, `node_modules/`, virtualenvs, large datasets or model weights, build artifacts. Add them to `.gitignore` as soon as they appear.
- **After every push** check the `[entire] Pushing … checkpoint ref(s)` line appeared.

## 4. How agents should work here

**Before starting a task**
1. Read this README, `README-Human` and **`VISION.md`** (our product idea, shared context for everyone); look at `Concept/` for the architecture sketch (`root.drawio`).
2. `git pull` and check what others (human or agent) are doing:
   - `entire recap` — summary of recent checkpoint activity
   - `entire session list`

- Color lives in the stripes. Everything else is ink on paper. Don't tint cards, panels or buttons.
- A chosen or active thing turns **solid ink with white text**. A not-chosen thing turns **muted**
  and keeps a ghost line to it. It stays visible and clickable.

## Type

- Face: **BMW Type Next** (licensed; used when installed or put in `gui/fonts/`, which is
  gitignored). Fallback: `system-ui` (SF on a Mac). Stack: `--type` in `start.css`.
- Large display text is light weight (300) with tight leading (≈1.05) and negative tracking
  (−0.025em). Example: the page title at 44px.
- Labels and option names are **bold UPPERCASE** with positive tracking (+0.04 to +0.08em), at
  11–15px. Section eyebrows are 11px, bold, uppercase, `--muted`.
- Body text is 13–14px with leading ≈1.5, in `--muted` for explanations.
- Show hierarchy through weight, size and case together, never size alone.

## Shapes and layout

- **Square corners** everywhere (radius 0). No shadows, no gradients, no rounded pills.
- **Hairline rules**, not boxes. A 2px ink rule on top of an option is its "landing pad" for the
  stripes. A 1px ink rule closes a title block, and `--hair` separates the quieter parts.
- **Editorial grid:** a left column (≈280px) holds titles and numbered step labels (ink circle
  with the number). The right column holds the flow. Generous vertical space: 96px of bend room
  (`FORK`) above every row.
- **Cards sit above the stripes** (`z-index`, `--paper` background), so the stripes appear to
  run *through* them.
- At phone width (≤800px) there is one column. The title covers the stripes' start, and labels
  sit left of the bundle with the bend room below them. No horizontal scroll.

## The stripes (how to draw them)

- There are 3 stripes, each 10px wide, touching (no gaps), with butt caps, in the order light
  blue, dark blue, red.
- Paths run vertically: straight down, then a cubic S-bend in the last `FORK` px before a
  target.
- Apply the offsets **along the curve's normal**, not sideways, so a bundle keeps its full
  width through bends (`curve()` in `start.js`).
- Assign stripes to targets **in order** (`floor(i * targets / 3)`), so they never cross.
- One target: all three pass through it, side by side. Several targets: they split and later
  rejoin.
- Options that aren't taken get a 1.5px `--ghost` line from the bundle.

## Motion

- Use **springs, not timed tweens**, for anything that moves because of the user: critically
  damped (damping 1.0), response ≈0.45s. X, Y and offset each spring independently.
- **Always start from the current on-screen value.** A new click mid-animation re-targets the
  motion, so it never jumps and never locks input.
- New parts **grow out of where the flow is**. A new stripe segment starts at the previous
  card's exit.
- Press feedback is instant on pointer-down: `:active { transform: scale(.97) }` over 100ms.
- Reveals: opacity plus a 14px rise, about 500ms, ease `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`, starting
  ~140ms after the stripes so the flow leads.
- Leaving a screen means materializing out: opacity, a slight scale-up (1.015) and blur, 450ms.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: springs snap and transitions become short fades. Nothing else
  changes.

## Interaction

- One choice per row, and the next row opens only when it's needed. Scroll it into view
  (`block: "nearest"`).
- Every earlier choice stays changeable (agency and forgiveness). There are no confirmation
  dialogs.
- Validate inline. Put the message in `--m-red` under the action, and focus the field that
  needs fixing.
- Use direct, specific labels ("Start agent", "Your CSV", "What should the agent work out?").
- Keyboard: real `<button>`s with `aria-pressed`, a visible `--m-light` focus ring, and `inert`
  on everything hidden or behind an overlay.

## Don't

- Don't use the BMW roundel or the M logo. The brand is evoked by the stripe colors only.
- Don't add color outside the stripes, or decoration that doesn't carry meaning.
- Don't use rounded corners, drop shadows or dashboard-style chrome.
- Don't use CSS keyframe animation for things the user drives (they can't be interrupted).

## 4. How agents should work here

**Before starting a task**
1. Read this README, `README-Human` and **`VISION.md`** (our product idea, shared context for everyone); look at `Concept/` for the architecture sketch (`root.drawio`).
2. `git pull` and check what others (human or agent) are doing:
   - `entire recap` — summary of recent checkpoint activity
   - `entire session list` — active/past agent sessions
   - `entire checkpoint search "<topic>"` — has someone already tried this?
3. Confirm the task is not already in progress to avoid duplicate work.

**While working**
- Keep scope tight: do the requested task, nothing more. Hackathon time is the scarcest resource.
- Prefer simple, working solutions over clever ones; a reliable demo beats extra features.
- Match existing structure, naming, and style. Don't introduce new frameworks or languages without team agreement.
- Keep the app runnable at every commit. If you break `main`, fixing it is the top priority.
- Document how to run anything you add (see §6) in the same commit.
- Use `entire agent-help` for machine-readable, version-accurate CLI usage instead of guessing commands.

**Handing off / resuming**
- Use `entire session resume <branch>` or `entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>` to pick up someone else's context instead of re-deriving it.
- `entire dispatch` produces a summary of recent agent work — use it for handoffs and pitch prep.

**When unsure** about requirements or the challenge brief: ask the team; challenge questions go to the partners on **Discord** (https://discord.gg/4UDNd5TAg). Do not assume partner support is available overnight.

## 5. LLMs, keys, and resources

- **OpenAI** is a tech partner: each participant has **75 USD** of LLM/API credits. Use them for app-level LLM calls.
- Keys go in a local `.env` (gitignored) and are read via environment variables; provide a `.env.example` with placeholder names only.
- Be mindful of token spend; `entire session tokens <id>` / `entire checkpoint tokens <id>` show usage.

## 6. Demo & submission readiness
# Design language — "M stripes as flow"

Approved by the team on the start screen (`start.js`, `start.css`, open `/ui/?start`). Every new
GUI page (graph view, mid-process view) follows these rules. Two references shaped it: the BMW M
stripes and editorial Sankey diagrams (black ribbons and labels on warm paper). Motion and craft
follow Apple's fluid-interface principles (WWDC "Designing Fluid Interfaces").

## The idea in one line

**The three M stripes are the flow of reasoning.** They run together as a bundle and fan out where
there's a choice. They pass *through* what was chosen and lead on to the next step. A line
always means "this came from that", the same meaning as an edge in the decision graph.

## Color

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--paper` | `#f4f3ef` | Page background (warm, not white) |
| `--ink` | `#111111` | Text, chosen cards, primary button, hairlines that matter |
| `--muted` | `#77746c` | Secondary text, unchosen options |
| `--hair` | `#d9d6ce` | Quiet dividers |
| `--ghost` | `#c9c5bb` | Thin lines to options that weren't taken |
| `--m-light` | `#1ea7e8` | Stripe 1; focus ring |
| `--m-dark` | `#1d2a8c` | Stripe 2 |
| `--m-red` | `#e4161f` | Stripe 3; errors |

- Color lives in the stripes. Everything else is ink on paper. Don't tint cards, panels or buttons.
- A chosen or active thing turns **solid ink with white text**. A not-chosen thing turns **muted**
  and keeps a ghost line to it. It stays visible and clickable.

// One column per stage of the chain, left to right. Decisions are not drawn as nodes:
// the GUI shows them as a verdict on their target instead.
export const STAGE = {
  Source: 0, Evidence: 1, Claim: 2, Assumption: 2, Requirement: 3, Score: 4, Question: 5, Note: 5,
};
export const DX = 260;
export const DY = 90;

/** {id: {x, y}}: each node sits at the mean height of its inputs, pushed down to avoid overlaps. */
export function layout(nodes, edges) {
  const inputsOf = {};
  for (const e of edges) (inputsOf[e.from_id] ??= []).push(e.to_id);

  const columns = {};
  for (const n of nodes) if (n.type in STAGE) (columns[STAGE[n.type]] ??= []).push(n);

  const pos = {};
  for (const stage of Object.keys(columns).map(Number).sort((a, b) => a - b)) {
    const wanted = columns[stage].map((n, i) => {
      const ys = (inputsOf[n.id] || []).filter((id) => pos[id]).map((id) => pos[id].y);
      return { id: n.id, y: ys.length ? ys.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / ys.length : i * DY };
    }).sort((a, b) => a.y - b.y);
    let floor = -Infinity;
    for (const w of wanted) {
      floor = Math.max(w.y, floor + DY);
      pos[w.id] = { x: stage * DX, y: floor };
    }
  }
  return pos;
}

## Graph view (`app.js`)

- **Columns flow left to right** (Source → Evidence → Claim → Requirement), like a Sankey.
- **Every link is a thin `--ghost` S-curve.** The selected node's chain lights up as the three
  stripes. Bundles stack on a card's side in the order they go (no crossings) and narrow when
  many share a side.
- **Nodes are ink-on-paper cards:** a top rule, then `TYPE · ID` in uppercase with a state tag on
  the right, then a 2-line title. Selected or approved: solid ink. States have no tinted fills:
  - stale: `--m-red` rule and tag;
  - postponed: dashed rule;
  - rejected or old version: muted, with a ghost rule;
  - waiting: a `NEEDS YOU` or `AGENT NEXT` tag.
